toegepas.voor: Sy graf het nog niemand gevind nie.
toegepas.na: Maar sy graf was nog nie gevind nie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: With the object first, a child can read it as 'his grave had not yet found anyone'; the passive is unambiguous and fits the past narrative.
toegepas.fout: With the object first, 'Sy graf het nog niemand gevind nie' can first be read as the grave not having found anyone.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The passive removes the misreading, says the same thing (the grave had not yet been found), and 'Maar' only makes explicit the contrast already there with the objects found.

toegepas.na: Daarom het rowers die graf gemis
toegepas.rede_vinder: The nearest antecedent of 'dit' is 'ingang', not the grave; naming the grave makes the reference clear and matches the lesson title.
toegepas.fout: 'dit' follows 'die klein graf se ingang' and could point to the entrance or to the grave.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the grave fixes the ambiguous pronoun without changing the meaning, and the later 'dit' in the same sentence then clearly refers to the grave too.

laat_vaar.voor: met hulle in die graf gesit
laat_vaar.na: met hulle in hul grafte gesit
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The subject is plural (earlier pharaohs), so the singular 'die graf' reads as one shared grave; 'hul grafte' matches the plural.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The distributive singular 'in die graf' after a plural subject is natural Afrikaans and reads as each pharaoh's own grave, so the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: maar nie almal vir farao's nie
laat_vaar.na: maar nie almal was vir farao's nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The elliptical clause lacks a verb and reads clipped; adding 'was' makes it a complete, natural clause for Grade 5.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'maar nie almal vir farao's nie' is natural, easy Afrikaans, and adding 'was' brings a tense mismatch with the present 'Daar is'.

laat_vaar.voor: voorwerpe gevind met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun).
laat_vaar.na: voorwerpe met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun) gevind.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Afrikaans places the past participle at the end of the clause; 'gevind met die naam van' is English word order. Protected names stay intact.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Placing a long prepositional phrase after the participle is accepted Afrikaans, and the proposal pushes 'gevind' behind the name and its English bracket, which is harder for a Grade 5 reader.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Hul' is the usual written possessive form; 'hulle' as possessive is more spoken.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Possessive 'hulle' is standard written Afrikaans, so swapping it for 'hul' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In written Afrikaans the subordinating conjunction is 'totdat'; 'tot' as a conjunction is colloquial.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot' is standard Afrikaans as a conjunction and reads naturally here, so 'totdat' is a lateral move.
